strategy.summary: Reproduce pandas CSV numeric inference overflow bug (pandas-dev/pandas#62813) by running the added regression test that exercises lib.maybe_convert_numeric on object arrays containing values at/above 2^64, and ensure the test fails on the buggy commit and passes on the fixed revision.

pinned_because: numpy pinned to 1.24.1 (documented numerically relevant constraint)
Cython is required to build pandas from sources but no version constraint was provided; choose any compatible Cython version available (unbounded in evidence)

strategy.reproducing_test: pandas/tests/dtypes/test_inference.py::TestConvertIntOverflow::test_convert_numeric_overflow (the newly added test in the diff)
strategy.success_criterion: The test should FAIL on the buggy revision (commit 27368892d374) and PASS on the fixed revision corresponding to PR #62813, because maybe_convert_numeric should produce the expected dtype/value array: for overflow inputs (including str(1<<65) and f"-{1<<65}"), buggy code leaves results as strings/object or incorrect conversions, while fixed code converts to Python ints when coerce_numeric=False using object dtype, and to float when coerce_numeric=True.
strategy.numerical_probe: Use the exact overflow inputs encoded by the test: value in [-(1<<65), (1<<65), str(1<<65), f"-{1<<65}"] and compare returned array against expected array with dtype float if coerce_numeric else object. This probes conversion around and above 2^64 (2^65 and signed variants).

input_output_examples.input: N/A (unit test calls lib.maybe_convert_numeric directly on np.array([value], dtype=object))
input_output_examples.buggy_output: On the buggy revision, at least one parameterization yields a result array not equal to expected (dtype and/or element values), making tm.assert_numpy_array_equal fail.
input_output_examples.expected_output: On the fixed revision, for all parameterizations and for both coerce_numeric in [False, True], tm.assert_numpy_array_equal passes with expected=np.array([expected_value], dtype=float if coerce_numeric else object).

risks: This strategy targets the internal regression test added in the PR diff (lib.maybe_convert_numeric). It does not directly run the read_csv integration test, so it assumes the bug is captured at this lower level by PR#62813.
The evidence does not specify the exact fixed commit SHA; you must run the test on the corresponding post-PR revision to observe the PASS transition.

Cython version is unbounded in the evidence; using an incompatible Cython/pandas build toolchain could prevent building or slightly change behavior. If the test cannot be built/run, report the build failure as a risk.

If the bug only manifests under the CSV parser path (engine-dependent) rather than in maybe_convert_numeric, this unit test may pass even on a regression; however the provided diff shows the intended fix and direct regression coverage at the conversion layer.

oracle.reference_source: Test expectations embedded in pandas/tests/dtypes/test_inference.py::test_convert_numeric_overflow from the provided diff (expected dtype and values are constructed as float if coerce_numeric else object).
oracle.why: The test uses tm.assert_numpy_array_equal with explicitly constructed expected arrays (dtype-controlled), so passing requires exact equality of both dtype and elements.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: The assertion tm.assert_numpy_array_equal(result, expected) fails for at least one (value, coerce_numeric) case on commit 27368892d374 because maybe_convert_numeric does not convert overflow inputs as intended (e.g., string overflow inputs stay as strings/object instead of becoming Python ints, or dtype conversion is otherwise incorrect).
strategy.passes_on_fixed: tm.assert_numpy_array_equal passes for all parameterizations: overflow values convert to Python ints in the object array when coerce_numeric=False, and to float values when coerce_numeric=True, matching expected exactly.
